+# Iteration 0.010 · n = 4 of 99 · 2026-09-24 · author: twelve lenses · round 4
+
+## Twelve lenses
+
+### Aset
+SSSES (business case): security 81 · stability 68 · scalability 65 · efficiency 65 · succinctness 62
+
+Founder, investors, customers: the record held its shape through the eleven-year edit. The ladder reads in the same order on S1, S2, S11, S15, S16 and S17; the one-ninth gate and alerting-last appear wherever absorption is named; the declared model is stated in the same words on S3, S8 and S15. What the previous rounds asked for, the record now carries. Two echoes remain, and I name them rather than fix them: S14 and S17 both restate the four horizons, and S12 and S14 both list the cost-to-serve items. Neither overflows. A theme is reinforced when each appearance adds a fact. Hold the register to that rule as the rounds continue.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Asar
+SSSES (business case): security 80 · stability 67 · scalability 66 · efficiency 64 · succinctness 60
+
+Read end to end, the deck delivers a whole: a leadership record that turns facts into named decisions, a benchmark carried inside it by qualification, a declared model with eleven funded years, a positive proxy return at gate weighting, and a register that says who decided what and when. What it lacked until this round was a calendar. Two rows on S16 said date TBD; a plan without a quarter is a wish. This round derives the G2 tabletop and the G3 trial from the row's own first-revenue quarter, labelled as assumptions. For the founder the synthesis is one question to an EDU president; for investors it is a dated sequence.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Athena
+SSSES (business case): security 80 · stability 69 · scalability 66 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 62
+
+Strategy is sequence plus calendar. Round two asked for a date on the G2 tabletop and a named institution. The institution cannot be invented and is not; the date can be derived and now is. The row says first revenue in the third quarter of 2027 and six paying accounts that year, so the measurement-design tabletop must close by the fourth quarter of 2026 and the instrumented trial by the first half of 2027, or the ramp is fiction. Both targets go on S16, marked as assumptions, with the gate each must pass. Investors can check the plan against a clock. Customers see when they would be asked to take part.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Christo
+SSSES (business case): security 79 · stability 67 · scalability 66 · efficiency 63 · succinctness 63
+
+The people a decision touches are on the page, and this round they answer back on the slide, not only in the note. On S4 the community that receives the alert replies, and the reply enters the record as operational truth. That is the difference between broadcasting at people and governing with them. The same loop serves a public body: a government asks its people through the polling interface, decides with named authority, and shows them what was decided and why, replayable by the body and by the citizens it serves. Founder, that is your moat; investors, it is a market no incumbent holds; customers, it is coherence that includes you.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Enki
+SSSES (business case): security 78 · stability 66 · scalability 64 · efficiency 62 · succinctness 61
+
+Edge cases keep the case honest. The platform's own outage during the event it serves has a degraded mode; the recall that crosses regulators and franchisees at once is on S4; the technical incident whose restoration minutes the platform must never claim is fenced on four slides. This round I looked for the edge not yet drawn: a public body adopting the loop for a project that is not a crisis at all, a road, a school, a budget. The shape holds because nothing in it is crisis-specific: facts, judgment, approval, owner, evidence, outcome, replay. The dependency goes on S13 as a speaker note, named as an assumption, not a claim.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Enlil
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 70 · scalability 67 · efficiency 68 · succinctness 63
+
+Buildability, as the builder reads it. Horizon 1 is seven objects and their screens; every one is a data model, not a research problem. The eleven-year record funds a build team for three years and a sustain team after that, which is the right shape for a product that earns each absorbed function by qualification. Round two left open the approver's identity. A named human on every consequence is only as strong as the proof that the human was the one who signed. This round adds the approver threat model to Horizon 1 on S14: step-up identity per approval, succession of decision rights, privilege-aware fields. Ship those with the seven objects.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Krishna
+SSSES (business case): security 81 · stability 68 · scalability 68 · efficiency 65 · succinctness 62
+
+Integration is where one-platform claims break, so I traced every feed again after the eleven-year edit. Nothing moved. Rave, the benchmark, PagerDuty, quality and recall systems, security and status pages enter as selected facts by pointer; the platform owns judgment, approval, owner and record; the export at end of life hands everything back in an open format. This round adds the one connection the brief now requires: the polling interface as the inbound feed from citizens and the outbound proof to them, so a public body's project runs on the same record as an institution's crisis. Investors see one architecture serving two markets. Customers see one login, one record, one exit.
+
+words: 111
+
+### Odin
+SSSES (business case): security 80 · stability 68 · scalability 70 · efficiency 64 · succinctness 63
+
+Read this in 2525 and the sentence about memory still parses, and now the calendar beneath it does, because each target is derived from a stated input rather than typed by hand. That is how a document outlives its tools: change the input, the deck re-derives, the register records why. Foresight for the founder: the incumbent will bundle a leadership module within three years; own the decision record and the C-suite door first. Foresight for investors: the second market is not a second product. A government that steers a public project through the same loop, with its citizens' answers in the record, is the platform's largest customer and its strongest proof.
+
+words: 111

+### Pangu
+SSSES (business case): security 78 · stability 66 · scalability 68 · efficiency 63 · succinctness 61
+
+The new thing remains the instrument, not a feature: the same scenario run twice, benchmark alone against the one platform, with hypothesis, null and stop rule declared before the clock starts. This round the instrument gains a date and a second use. The date makes it an experiment with a calendar entry, not a promise. The second use is the one the brief opened: a public body can rehearse a policy posture the same way before adopting it, and its citizens can replay what was decided and why. Investors fund a device that keeps earning its place; customers get a platform that proves itself function by function, on its own clock.
+
+words: 111

+### Sofia
+SSSES (business case): security 79 · stability 67 · scalability 65 · efficiency 64 · succinctness 63
+
+Seven readers, one page, checked again. The demo audience gets sentence, loop and ladder from S1. The customer gets a single-customer baseline and now the quarter they would be asked to take part. The innovator finds the inputs the linked fields derive from and the register that says why each decision was made. The investor sees a labelled ramp, eleven funded years and a positive proxy return. The business owner sees the value equation, one line per term. The system thinker reads clocks in minutes and risks as ranges. The execution genius reads what ships in 2027, what qualifies by 2030, and now the approver's identity model beside the seven objects.

+words: 111

+### Thoth
+SSSES (business case): security 82 · stability 70 · scalability 66 · efficiency 67 · succinctness 62
+
+The numbers reconcile after the eleven-year edit, and the gate asserts it: the row's spend and revenue are the roll-up of the plan, the account-years sum to the ramp, the four value drivers sum to the modeled value, the proxy return is positive at gate weighting. This round I checked the calendar against the record. Six paying accounts in 2027 with first revenue in the third quarter require a measurement design proven by the end of 2026 and a trial closed by mid-2027; the S16 targets are derived from that, not chosen. My ask stands: when the trial verifies one minute value, replace one input and let the deck re-derive everything.
+
+words: 111

+### Thor
+SSSES (business case): security 84 · stability 69 · scalability 65 · efficiency 63 · succinctness 61
+
+Risk, as the guardian reads it. The four that matter are on S13 with a mitigation each: the platform's own outage, the appearance of a machine commanding, the data boundary, and simulation as theatre. Round two named the fifth and this round writes it in: the record is only as trustworthy as the identity behind each approval. Step-up identity on every consequential sign-off, succession of decision rights when the approver is unreachable, privilege-aware fields for what counsel marks, all as Horizon-1 deliverables on S14. For a public body the stakes are higher, since its citizens replay the record; the same controls are the price of that transparency. Nothing else has weakened.
